findings.title: Team admin/owner check requires both roles instead of either
findings.body: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed as isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...). A team admin who is not the owner, and an owner whose admin check does not also return true, therefore fail this test. Unless such a user is also the booking organizer or an attendee, legitimate team admins/owners are incorrectly rejected with FORBIDDEN when adding guests. The condition should be an OR.

findings.title: Any attendee account can add arbitrary guests and disclose the meeting
findings.body: Authorization accepts any booking attendee whose account email matches an attendee email. That attendee can then add arbitrary email addresses; the handler adds them to the booking, updates the calendar event, and sends new guests an AttendeeScheduledEmail containing the event details and joining information. An attendee therefore does not need organizer or team-admin approval to expand access to a private meeting. This endpoint is also directly callable through tRPC even though the new UI is on the organizer bookings page.

findings.title: Guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, pending, or past bookings
findings.body: After checking that the booking exists, the handler never checks booking.status or whether the booking is still upcoming. It creates attendees, calls updateCalendarAttendees, and sends scheduled/add-guests emails even for cancelled or rejected bookings and for events that have already ended. The UI also exposes booked actions for past confirmed bookings. This can resurrect calendar invites and meeting emails for events that should no longer accept guests.

findings.title: Server schema allows duplicate, empty-sized, and unbounded guest lists
findings.body: The server input is only z.array(z.string().email()): it has no uniqueness constraint, minimum, or maximum. The handler's filter only compares each guest with the booking's pre-existing attendees, so guests:['a@example.com','a@example.com'] creates two attendee rows for the same person, and case variants such as A@example.com/a@example.com also bypass both attendee and blacklist comparisons (the blacklist is lower-cased but guests are not). A caller bypassing the client dialog can also submit thousands of guests, causing bulk attendee creation, calendar updates, and emails. Enforce a bounded, case-normalized unique set on the server and pass that normalized set to sendAddGuestsEmails instead of raw guests.

findings.title: Calendar is updated using the caller's credentials rather than the organizer's
findings.body: getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) and the EventManager are built from the authenticated caller. When the caller is an attendee or a team admin rather than booking.userId, updateCalendarAttendees is attempted with the wrong user's calendar/video credentials (or none), so the organizer's calendar event is not reliably updated with the new attendees even though the database rows were already created and success may be reported. The EventManager should be constructed for the booking organizer, as the calendar event belongs to that user.

findings.title: MultiEmail imports from its own package index, creating a circular import
findings.body: This file lives inside @calcom/ui but imports Button, EmailField, Icon, and Tooltip from '@calcom/ui'. The package index exports MultiEmail from MultiEmailLazy, which dynamically imports this file, so the module graph cycles back through the partially initialized package entry point. Depending on bundling/chunking this can yield undefined components at runtime. Import these components via their relative paths inside packages/ui instead of the package self-reference.
